content: The absorption of tetracyclines may be impaired by products containing multivalent cations, potentially reducing their effectiveness. To mitigate this, the administration of tetracyclines should be separated from these products. Specifically: 1. Ferumoxytol reduces the absorption of sarecycline in the gastrointestinal tract, decreasing its levels or effects. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 2. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of drugs such as fexofenadine, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, hydrocortisone, idarubicin, imatinib, indinavir, ivermectin, lapatinib, ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, lenvatinib, linagliptin, loperamide, loratadine, lovastatin, maraviroc, methotrexate, mitomycin, morphine, nadolol, naldemedine, nelfinavir, nicardipine, nilotinib, nintedanib, ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir, ondansetron, osimertinib, paclitaxel, paclitaxel protein-bound, paliperidone, pazopanib, pomalidomide, posaconazole, pravastatin, prednisone, quinidine, quinine, ranolazine, rifampin, rifaximin, riociguat, risperidone, ritonavir, saxagliptin, silodosin, simvastatin, sirolimus, sitagliptin, sofosbuvir, tacrolimus, temsirolimus, teniposide, tenofovir AF, tenofovir DF, testosterone, tolvaptan, topotecan, trabectedin, velpatasvir, vemurafenib, venetoclax, verapamil, vinblastine, vincristine, and vincristine liposomal. These interactions occur via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring for toxicities is necessary, as dosage reductions may be required. 3. Iodine, iron dextran complex, iron sucrose, iron/folic acid/vitamin/mineral supplements, magnesium chloride, magnesium citrate, magnesium gluconate, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium oxide, magnesium supplements, manganese, molybdenum, multivitamins, multivitamins with vision support, polysaccharide iron, sodium acid phosphate, sodium bicarbonate, sodium citrate/citric acid, sodium phosphate rectal, sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid, trimagnesium citrate anhydrous, and tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate reduce the absorption of sarecycline in the gastrointestinal tract, decreasing its levels or effects. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. For magnesium-containing products, administer magnesium 2 hours before or 4 hours after tetracycline administration to avoid the formation of insoluble complexes that reduce drug absorption.
